content.text:
Fixed. Two changes, plus a regression test.

**The bug.** `lib/interceptor/cache.js` only skipped *safe* methods that weren't in `opts.methods`; unsafe methods (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) fell through into the full caching path. That meant two things:

- `store.get(cacheKey)` was called with an unsafe-method cache key, so a stored entry for e.g. `POST /x` would be replayed instead of hitting the origin.
- `CacheHandler.onResponseStart` only short-circuited unsafe methods on status 200–399 (the invalidation branch). An unsafe-method response with a status ≥ 400 skipped that branch and went into the normal storing logic — so a `POST` answered with, say, `404` plus `cache-control: max-age=60` (or just `last-modified`, since 404/405/410/414/501 are heuristically cacheable) was written to the cache store.

**The fix.**

- `lib/interceptor/cache.js:627` — unsafe methods now go straight to `dispatch(opts, new CacheHandler(...))`, so the cache is never read for them, while they still pass through `CacheHandler` for invalidation.
- `lib/handler/cache-handler.js:209` — the unsafe-method branch now always returns after (conditionally) invalidating, so a response to an unsafe method is never stored regardless of status code or caching directives.

Successful unsafe-method invalidation is untouched: the 200–399 case still calls `invalidateUnsafeRequest`, including the `Location` / `Content-Location` purging.

**Verification.** All 89 tests in `test/interceptors/cache.js` pass, including the existing `unsafe methods cause resource to be purged from cache` and the Location/Content-Location purge tests; the cache-adjacent suites (`cache-async-store`, `cache-query-params`, `cache-revalidate-stale`, `deduplicate`, `test/cache-interceptor/*`) pass — 165 tests, 0 failures. The new test (`test/interceptors/cache.js:1094`) drives POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE against a 404 + `max-age=60` origin with a store whose `get`/`createWriteStream` both `fail()`, and asserts all four requests reached the origin.

Two caveats on what I did *not* verify: I could not demonstrate the new test failing against the pre-fix code — reverting the files temporarily and extracting a scratch copy of `HEAD` both required approvals that were declined — so the pre-fix analysis above is from reading the code, not from an executed red test. I also couldn't run `eslint` on the changed files (approval declined); the changes follow the surrounding style but are unlinted. Nothing is committed.

result:
Fixed. Two changes, plus a regression test.

**The bug.** `lib/interceptor/cache.js` only skipped *safe* methods that weren't in `opts.methods`; unsafe methods (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) fell through into the full caching path. That meant two things:

- `store.get(cacheKey)` was called with an unsafe-method cache key, so a stored entry for e.g. `POST /x` would be replayed instead of hitting the origin.
- `CacheHandler.onResponseStart` only short-circuited unsafe methods on status 200–399 (the invalidation branch). An unsafe-method response with a status ≥ 400 skipped that branch and went into the normal storing logic — so a `POST` answered with, say, `404` plus `cache-control: max-age=60` (or just `last-modified`, since 404/405/410/414/501 are heuristically cacheable) was written to the cache store.

**The fix.**

- `lib/interceptor/cache.js:627` — unsafe methods now go straight to `dispatch(opts, new CacheHandler(...))`, so the cache is never read for them, while they still pass through `CacheHandler` for invalidation.
- `lib/handler/cache-handler.js:209` — the unsafe-method branch now always returns after (conditionally) invalidating, so a response to an unsafe method is never stored regardless of status code or caching directives.

Successful unsafe-method invalidation is untouched: the 200–399 case still calls `invalidateUnsafeRequest`, including the `Location` / `Content-Location` purging.

**Verification.** All 89 tests in `test/interceptors/cache.js` pass, including the existing `unsafe methods cause resource to be purged from cache` and the Location/Content-Location purge tests; the cache-adjacent suites (`cache-async-store`, `cache-query-params`, `cache-revalidate-stale`, `deduplicate`, `test/cache-interceptor/*`) pass — 165 tests, 0 failures. The new test (`test/interceptors/cache.js:1094`) drives POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE against a 404 + `max-age=60` origin with a store whose `get`/`createWriteStream` both `fail()`, and asserts all four requests reached the origin.

Two caveats on what I did *not* verify: I could not demonstrate the new test failing against the pre-fix code — reverting the files temporarily and extracting a scratch copy of `HEAD` both required approvals that were declined — so the pre-fix analysis above is from reading the code, not from an executed red test. I also couldn't run `eslint` on the changed files (approval declined); the changes follow the surrounding style but are unlinted. Nothing is committed.
